international.title: First Thing: Peltola’s Alaska victory secures 56th Democratic seat in Senate
international.summary: The ninth gain of the midterms in the upper chamber, it is the first time Alaska has elected a Democrat since 2008. Plus the impact the NAZA documentary is having inside Israel Good morning. Democrats will control 56 seats in the upper chamber after the final Senate race was called in favor of Mary Peltola . The party gained nine Senate seats in the midterms, a sweeping victory that will put them decisively back in the majority beginning next year. Peltola, a former US House lawmaker, is the first Democrat Alaska has elected to the Senate since 2008. Her campaign was dogged by controversy after the New York Times reported her staffers had helped recruit a second Republican challenger also named Dan Sullivan to run. Although Peltola’s team denied involvement, the alleged ruse prompted Donald Trump to call for her prosecution and triggered federal and state investigations. Continue reading...
